title: Ulyana and the Ember
premise: Freya Okafor, a bone-carver who hears the dead through the carvings she makes, lives in a valley where magic cannot follow — until her blind date, a historian named Tomas, arrives carrying a century-old prophecy book with tonight's date inked on its final page. The prophecy names Ulyana, the true king unbound from his body by the Ember, a parasitic flame wearing his crown, and names Tomas as the key to restoring him. Dragged out of the magicless valley, Freya must learn to weaponize her gift while deciding whether loyalty to the dead who guide her outweighs the truths they hide. She frees Ulyana at the cost of her own hearing, defeats the Ember before it reaches the free cities, and returns to the valley changed — no longer able to hear the dead, but finally able to live among the living.
about_author: Zephyrine Oyelaran is the pen name of a former mortuary archivist who spent six years cataloguing unclaimed remains before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about the obligations the living owe the dead, from a coastal town that keeps its own cemetery records by hand.

chapters.title: The Date and the Dead
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya carves a keepsake bone for a grieving widow, hearing the widow's dead husband whisper through the grain, then rushes to a blind date with Tomas, a soft-spoken historian. He arrives clutching an antique prophecy book open to tonight's date. Emotional beat: wary tenderness curdling into dread as the book names them both.

chapters.title: Ink That Wasn't There Yesterday
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas explains he bought the book a week ago; the final prophecy appeared overnight, written in ink that matches his own handwriting. It describes Freya by name and a king called Ulyana, bound beneath his own crown. Emotional beat: the vertigo of realizing your life was authored a century before you.

chapters.title: Where Magic Cannot Follow
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The prophecy's first line comes true: riders bearing the Ember's sigil reach the valley's border and cannot cross, so they burn the outlying farms instead. The dead in Freya's carvings scream a single instruction: take the historian and run. Emotional beat: guilt and fury as her sanctuary becomes a trap for everyone she's failed to protect.

chapters.title: Crossing the Silence
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Fleeing through the border, Tomas feels magic flood him for the first time — the book begins rewriting itself around his choices. Freya, cut off from the dead beyond the valley, is deafened by silence for the first time in her life. Emotional beat: mutual dependence born of mutual loss; the beginning of real trust.

chapters.title: The Court of Cinders
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. They reach the capital, where the Ember-crowned king rules through charm and ash. Freya carves a bone from a executed rebel and hears his ghost describe the ritual that bound Ulyana. Emotional beat: horror at how just the usurper's laws appear — justice inside the law serving monstrous ends.

chapters.title: What the Dead Withheld
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The ghosts guiding Freya have been lying by omission: the unbinding ritual requires a living anchor, and the prophecy's fine print names Tomas. Freya learns and says nothing. Emotional beat: the first fracture — loyalty to the dead versus truth to the living.

chapters.title: Armies on the Salt Road
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The Ember's armies march on the free cities, and the rebels beg Freya to delay the ritual until after the war, though every night of delay lets the Ember dig deeper into Ulyana. She must choose the sequence of two impossible urgencies. Emotional beat: the crushing arithmetic of survival — who can be saved, and when.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. In the crypt beneath the palace, Freya performs the ritual with Tomas as anchor, tearing the Ember from Ulyana's body. Tomas burns as the anchor — not to death, but to memory, forgetting Freya entirely. Emotional beat: triumph and heartbreak in the same breath; the price paid is not life but love.

chapters.title: The Ember's Last Argument
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The disembodied Ember offers Freya a bargain: her hearing restored, Tomas's memory returned, if she lets it take a new crown — hers. Freya refuses and, using the dead's final chorus, shatters it. Ulyana, freed, rides to break the siege. Emotional beat: the climax of the loyalty-versus-truth theme; she chooses truth at permanent cost.

chapters.title: A Quiet Grain of Bone
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, coda. The free cities hold; Ulyana rules a kingdom learning justice beyond vengeance. Freya returns to the valley, her gift gone, and finds Tomas — who doesn't know her but asks her to stay for dinner anyway. She carves one last bone and hears nothing, and it sounds like peace. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution; survival's price paid, and worth it.
